description_summary: 12-month unduplicated student headcounts broken down by undergraduate or graduate level, sex, and nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV).

12-month instructional activity measured as total credit hours and/or contact hours delivered, reported for undergraduate and graduate instruction. These measures support calculation of 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment; the description does not specify additional row-identifier variables.

Academic library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services for degree-granting institutions, covering the 2016-17 reporting period in the 2017-18 file. The table is institution/library-level, with one record per eligible institution; expenditure data are available only for degree-granting institutions whose total expenditures exceed $100,000. The Academic Libraries survey has been part of IPEDS since 2014-15.

Institution-level data for Fall 2017 undergraduate admissions of first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking students at institutions that do not have an open-admission policy. The table includes admission consideration factors, applicant counts, admitted applicants, admitted students who enrolled, and SAT/ACT scores when tests are required for admission; SAT and ACT writing scores are not collected. Each institution is the record grain, with admission-consideration variables and applicant, admission, enrollment, and test-score measures.

Awards conferred broken down by six-digit CIP program, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, and contains award totals plus gender and race/ethnicity detail.

Students receiving at least one degree or certificate, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. This is one record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID, and counts students rather than awards, with totals and gender-by-race/ethnicity detail.

Students receiving degrees or certificates broken down by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age category. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age groups are under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age are reported as separate breakdowns rather than combined categories.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education, broken down by CIP program and award level rather than by student demographics. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE: six-digit CIP records identify award levels offered and offered via distance education, two-digit CIP records summarize the six-digit programs within the CIP group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID plus attendance status and student level (EFLEVEL), with total, male, and female enrollment counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID plus attendance status and student level (EFALEVEL); enrollment is provided for all nine race/ethnicity categories as well as total, male, and female counts.

Fall enrollment counts by distance-education status and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and student level (EFDELEV), with totals for students exclusively in distance education, in some distance education, or in none; exclusively distance-education students are further categorized by location as the same state/jurisdiction, a different state/jurisdiction, the U.S. with unknown state/jurisdiction, or outside the U.S.

Fall enrollment counts by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Age enrollment is optional for institutions to report in even-numbered years; because 2017 is odd-numbered, this table has age data for 2017.

First-time freshman counts by state of residence, including the number who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Residence enrollment is optional for institutions to report in odd-numbered years; because 2017 is odd-numbered, the table is available but may not include every institution.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, applicable only to institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions, and institutions with less-than-one-year programs do not have retention data; retention tracks the fall 2016 cohort into fall 2017.

Institutional fiscal-year finance records for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards. Each record is identified by institution (UNITID) and includes revenues, expenditures, endowments, assets, and liabilities; it is the appropriate form for public GASB institutions.

Institutional fiscal-year finance records for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards. Each record is identified by institution (UNITID) and includes revenues, expenditures, endowments, assets, and liabilities; it excludes public institutions reporting under GASB.

Institutional fiscal-year finance records for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards. Each record is identified by institution (UNITID) and includes revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities; endowment data are not included in this form.

Graduation outcomes measured at 200% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at four-year institutions with cohort year 2009 and less-than-4-year institutions with cohort year 2013. Records are institution-level and use UNITID and the cohort/graduation-status type (GRTYPE), reporting completion at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time; unlike gr2017, this table is not described as having gender or race/ethnicity detail. The table metadata gives a status date of August 31, 2017, while its description says August 31, 2016.

Graduation outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID, cohort/graduation-status type (GRTYPE), gender, and race/ethnicity; four-year records distinguish bachelor’s-degree seekers from other degree/certificate seekers, while two-year records include completion at 100% and 150% of normal time and transfers, but 100%-normal-time completion is unavailable by gender and race/ethnicity for two-year institutions.

Graduation outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment and completion within 100% or 150% of normal time and transfer-out status. The records are institution-level, identified by UNITID, with no gender, race/ethnicity, or financial-aid subcohort breakdown described.

Graduation outcomes at four-year, two-year, and less-than-2-year institutions divided into three financial-aid subcohorts: Pell Grant recipients; subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell; and students receiving neither. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and PSGRTYPE, and contain subcohort outcomes rather than gender or race/ethnicity breakdowns; four-year records distinguish bachelor’s-degree seekers from other degree/certificate seekers, while two-year and less-than-2-year records report 150%-normal-time completion.

Staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length for non-tenure-track staff. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, the occupational-category and tenure-status code.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with contract-length detail for non-tenure-track staff. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines faculty/tenure status with academic rank; race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2017 (odd) has data.

Full-time new hires at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender, with instructional new hires additionally classified by faculty/tenure status and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, the occupation and instructional faculty/tenure-status code; for Fall 2017, new hires are those hired for full-time permanent employment for the first time or after a break in service during November 1, 2016–October 31, 2017, rather than the pre-2017 July 1–October 31 window, and race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2017 (odd) has data.

Full- and part-time payroll staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, the occupational-category and full-/part-time-status code; race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2017 (odd) has data.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and, for non-tenure-track staff, contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, the faculty- and tenure-status code.

Counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated nine-month salary measures for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and number of months worked. The row-defining variables are UNITID and ARANK; staff working fewer than nine months have counts but no salary data.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical, noninstructional staff, broken down by occupational category; the records are institution-by-occupational-category observations.

Custom comparison-group membership records for the 2018 Data Feedback Report, keyed by the reporting institution and each comparison institution in its submitted group; includes the comparison institution’s UNITID, name, and state.

Response-status records keyed by institution (UNITID) and survey component, showing whether the component applies, was submitted, or has imputed data; also identifies parent/child reporting and revised component submissions. Use this table for component-level reporting status rather than institution directory attributes.

Institution directory records keyed by institution (UNITID), including identifying and contact information, web links, active status, Title IV participation, control and institutional level, highest award offerings, and Carnegie classifications.

Institution-level records keyed by UNITID covering educational offerings and award levels, organizational control and affiliations, admissions characteristics, special learning opportunities, and athletic associations.

Full-academic-year student-charge records for institutions whose primarily academic, credit-hour programs use a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendar. The grain is institution (UNITID), with separate charges for full-time and part-time undergraduate and graduate students, professional-practice programs, and first-time full-time undergraduate cost-of-attendance components.

Program-level student-charge records for institutions with clock-hour programs or primarily occupational credit-hour programs. Records identify the institution (UNITID), the number of programs, and charges for the largest program plus tuition and fees and books and supplies for up to five additional programs; this is the vocational-program alternative to the full-academic-year charges table.
Institution-level mission-statement records keyed by UNITID, containing either the mission statement text or a web address for it.

Award and enrollment outcomes for four 2009-10 entering undergraduate cohorts, each split by Pell-recipient status: first-time full-time, first-time part-time, non-first-time full-time, and non-first-time part-time. Degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates entering from July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, are included at degree-granting institutions; the table reports revised and adjusted cohort sizes and the numbers and percentages who completed or remained enrolled as of August 31, 2013 (four years), August 31, 2015 (six years), and August 31, 2017 (eight years). Records are uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort (OMCHRT), with multiple records per institution.

Student financial aid recipients and aid amounts, broken down by undergraduate population group and aid source/type. The row-defining variables are institution, population group—full-time first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates or all undergraduates—and aid category; the first group includes federal, Pell, other federal, state/local, institutional, and federal/nonfederal loan measures, while the all-undergraduate group includes total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans, with recipient counts, total dollars, and average dollars.

Average net price and its underlying financial-aid measures for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in two groups: grant or scholarship aid recipients and Title IV federal-aid recipients. The row-defining variables are institution and aid-recipient group; at public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying the in-district or in-state tuition rate.

Military, servicemember, and veteran benefit recipients and benefit amounts, broken down by student level and benefit program. The row-defining variables are institution, undergraduate or graduate status, and benefit type—Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits or the Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program.
